newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar on Thursday in dull trading, dealers said.

"The market continues to be very quiet and volume was low," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank. "The Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market (buying dollars) to support the basket after the U.S. currency rose abroad."
"The central bank intervened on a relatively small scale buying around $50 million," Zadka said.
The Bank of Israel has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for nearly two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3670 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6467 shekels against 3.6466 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7738 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7731 on Wednesday and against the mark at 1.9607 shekels against 1.9650 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3695 shekels.
